items.title: BYOK and enterprise custom models in the Copilot usage API
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: The Copilot usage metrics API now shows bring your own key (BYOK) usage across GitHub Copilot, so you can separate it from Copilot-hosted model usage. Reports cover two kinds of BYOK: Local BYOK is configured by developers in their client. Requests go from Copilot CLI or the GitHub Copilot app directly to the developer’s provider key or local model. Find it in used_local_byok, totals_by_local_byok, and active local BYOK user counts. Enterprise custom models are configured by admins in GitHub settings, and requests route through GitHub to your provider. Find them with is_custom_enterprise_model in totals_by_client. Both appear in enterprise and organization reports, at the user and aggregate level, in 1-day and 28-day reports. Local BYOK Local BYOK covers a developer’s own provider key and local models served by tools such as Ollama, Foundry Local, LM Studio, and llama-server. used_local_byok: Whether a user made at least one local BYOK request in Copilot CLI or the Copilot app that day. Appears in user-level reports. totals_by_local_byok: Session, request, prompt, and token counts, broken out by byok_kind (local_managed, local_user, local_auto, or remote_user) and surface (copilot_cli or copilot_app). Appears in user-level and aggregate reports. daily_active_local_byok_users, weekly_active_local_byok_users, and monthly_active_local_byok_users: Distinct users with local BYOK activity for the day, calendar week, and calendar month. Appears in aggregate reports. Enterprise custom models Added is_custom_enterprise_model, a boolean on each totals_by_client[].totals_by_model[] entry. Its value is true when the request used a custom model configured for your enterprise or organization. GitHub observes these requests server-side, so the field covers every client, including IDEs. A model used both as a Copilot-hosted model and as a custom model appears as two entries, so the counts stay separate. Custom model entries include real request and token counts. Why this matters BY
items.why_it_matters: Copilot usage API now separates BYOK and enterprise custom model usage. Useful for CTOs advising clients on Copilot cost tracking and governance, though First Mate's core tools are Claude Code and Codex.

items.title: CodeQL 2.27.4 improves accuracy and query metadata
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: CodeQL is the static analysis engine behind GitHub code scanning, which finds and remediates security issues in your code. We’ve recently released CodeQL 2.27.4 with query accuracy improvements across several languages, stronger security checks when you bundle or publish a pack, and corrections to query metadata. Query changes Java/Kotlin The java/log-injection query now recognizes additional sanitizers and sanitizer guards from the JDK, Apache Commons Lang and Text, Guava, OWASP Java Encoder, and Spring Framework. Path-injection queries now recognize additional substring guards and string replacement and removal operations from Apache Commons Lang and Guava. Rust We have reduced false positives in the rust/uncontrolled-allocation-size, rust/log-injection, and rust/cleartext-logging queries. C/C++ The cpp/suspicious-pointer-scaling query no longer reports intentional pointer arithmetic on std::byte* buffers. The cpp/unused-local-variable and cpp/unused-static-variable queries no longer report variables marked with [[maybe_unused]]. CWE metadata changes CodeQL no longer applies the CWE-730 tag to the following queries: C#: cs/redos and cs/regex-injection. Java/Kotlin: java/redos, java/polynomial-redos, and java/regex-injection. JavaScript/TypeScript: js/redos, js/polynomial-redos, js/regex-injection, js/regex-injection-more-sources, js/server-crash, and js/loop-bound-injection. Python: py/redos, py/polynomial-redos, and py/regex-injection. Ruby: rb/redos, rb/polynomial-redos, and rb/regexp-injection. Swift: swift/redos and swift/regex-injection. This was initially reported in CodeQL issue #22318; thank you to @wiggin15 for the feedback. CodeQL CLI The CLI now writes Java virtual machine warnings and initialization errors to standard error, so they won’t interfere with JSON or other machine-readable output. When you bundle or publish a pack, the CLI checks whether each file remains inside the pack root after resolving symbolic links. It omits files that resolve outsid
items.why_it_matters: CodeQL update improves code scanning accuracy and pack publishing security. Relevant to GitHub Actions security pipelines, though the highlighted changes are mostly for Java and Kotlin.

items.title: GitHub Copilot is now available in Xcode’s coding assistant
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: You can now work with GitHub Copilot directly in Xcode’s built-in coding assistant, bringing Copilot into your native Xcode workflow. The integration is now in public preview, available starting with Xcode 27.3 beta. This gives you another way to use Copilot in Xcode. The existing GitHub Copilot for Xcode extension remains a separate option, so you can choose the workflow that works best for you. Get started Download Xcode 27.3 beta from Apple Developer Downloads. You’ll need a Mac running macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later. In Xcode, open Xcode > Settings > Intelligence to set up GitHub Copilot in the coding assistant. For more information, see Setting up coding intelligence and the Xcode 27.3 beta release notes. All Copilot plans are supported. Share your feedback Help us improve the experience by sharing your feedback in the GitHub Copilot for Xcode repository or through Apple Feedback Assistant. The post GitHub Copilot is now available in Xcode’s coding assistant appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.why_it_matters: Copilot in Xcode's built-in assistant, in public preview. Of limited relevance to a web-focused Next.js and TypeScript studio that relies mainly on Claude Code and Codex.

items.title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?
items.author: eggbrain
items.excerpt: I'm curious how people on HN are using AI day to day, and came up with a list of questions I thought could be interesting to know. No need to answer every question of course, just wanted to get a gut feel how people are using AI.1) What AI subscriptions are you personally paying for? (Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Cursor, etc)- Which tiers?- Have you purchased multiple subscriptions from the same provider (eg two Claude accounts)?2) Are you using models outside (or instead) of those subscriptions? For example, pay-as-you-go APIs, OpenRouter, or locally hosted models.- Which models and providers?3) What coding harnesses and interfaces are you using? Are you sticking with the default CLIs or IDE integrations, or using alternatives like OpenCode, Pi, Aider, Muse Code, or custom-built harnesses?- What made you switch harnesses (if you switched)?4) Are you using any agent orchestration or swarm tools?- For example, Munder Difflin, Gas Town, Ruflo, or something custom.5) Are you using broader agent platforms like OpenClaw / Hermes Agent / Grok bot / Dots / Muse?- If you are using them, what are your main use cases?-----I know my workflow has differed significantly from a year ago, and so it would be interesting to capture a snapshot today of what people are using and why. items.title: datasette-apps 0.3a0
items.excerpt: Release: datasette-apps 0.3a0 Datasette Apps adds support for hosting and editing custom HTML applications inside of Datasette. These can be created by hand, but it's easier to create them using LLMs via Datasette Agent. This release improves that integration: Apps can now be tagged in Datasette Agent chat messages by typing #, which autocompletes from the apps the user has permission to view. New app_add_stored_queries() and app_remove_stored_queries() tools let the agent manage which stored queries an app is allowed to call. Granting a write query requires approval from the user first. app_create() now checks that each requested stored query exists and that the user can view it, and asks the user to approve any write queries before the app is created. The "View app" buttons shown by the agent tools, and the links on # app references, now open the app full screen in the Datasette Agent panel. Tags: datasette, datasette-agent, datasette-apps
